paragraphs.source_en: Sanada Saemon-no-Suke Yukimura was regarded as a complete heretic within Osaka Castle.

units.source_zh: 真田左卫门佐幸村完全被当成了大坂城内的异端。

paragraphs.source_en: But under the present circumstances, what could Yukimura possibly do? Should he break out from the Sanada enclosure, cut through Maeda's lines, and charge straight at Hidetada's headquarters—or silently submit to peace? If he chose the former, his entire force would surely be annihilated before it reached Hidetada's camp; if he chose the latter, what meaning had there been in entering the castle?

paragraphs.source_en: “The composure to respect one's opponent even amid a confused melee—that is what makes a true warrior.”

paragraphs.source_en: Yukimura did not answer. At the time, he had not conceived a desire to kill Naomasa because the images of Daisuke and his nephews had arisen in his mind, and the cruelty of war had stirred his compassion.

paragraphs.source_en: “Daisuke, all of this is for the Minister of the Right to decide. Once he has decided, no one else should offer needless objections. That too is the way of the warrior.”

paragraphs.source_en: “Yes. The Minister of the Right is far braver than I had imagined. If he makes his decision, I will obey without fail.”

paragraphs.source_en: When Yukimura reached the inner citadel, nearly all the commanders had assembled in the great hall, from which the tatami had been removed. Leading Daisuke along the corridor, Yukimura stepped with muddy feet upon the coarse reed mats and prayed silently. He asked only that the women, Lady Yodo foremost among them, not appear at today's assembly.

paragraphs.source_zh: 当幸村到达本城，诸将几都集于已揭去榻榻米的大厅内。幸村领着大助，穿过走廊，泥脚踏着粗糙的苇席，心里暗自祷告。他只求在今日的席上，以淀夫人为首的女人不要露面。

paragraphs.source_en: A man's pledge was worth a thousand pieces of gold, whereas women were easily swayed by emotion. Moreover, the women cared only about whether people lived or died. If the rōnin gathered in Osaka decided to cause trouble, there was no telling what disorder might follow.

units.source_en: A man's pledge was worth a thousand pieces of gold, whereas women were easily swayed by emotion.

units.source_en: Moreover, the women cared only about whether people lived or died.

paragraphs.source_en: But the instant Yukimura entered the hall, he could only sigh inwardly again and again—Hideyori was nowhere to be seen, yet seated to the left of the place of honor, accompanied by Senhime and the elderly women, was that not Lady Yodo, pale-faced and rigid as if frozen?

paragraphs.source_en: Those summoned included not only the commanders defending the inner citadel and the second and third wards, but also the eleven generals who had erected palisades outside the castle. paragraphs.source_en: Lady Yodo had already goaded Hideyori into making his decision. That being so, with a mighty enemy before them, arguing until their faces turned red would not alter the outcome. They could first make peace and wait until the Edo forces withdrew before deciding what to do next.

paragraphs.source_en: “You have all endured much.” Hideyori said after taking his seat. Having said this, he fell silent and squeezed his eyes shut. Tears welled from both eyes and traced several glistening paths down his cheeks.
